clue.text: Economise on part of line

parts.note: on, as in 'regarding', is RE
a trench is a section of a front line in trench warfare

explanation.surface: A railway company saves money by running trains on only part of a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests railways, but here it is a military front line, which was made up of trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back spending is to reduce costs, the usual sense of the verb.

clue.text: Girl a mere subject for Monet, often

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
a mere is a small lake, so a pond

explanation.surface: A young woman is described as nothing more than a model for the painter Monet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' reads as 'only', but it is the noun for a small lake. Monet painted his water garden at Giverny again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Monet's famous water-lily paintings show the pool in his garden, a painter's recurring motif.

clue.text: Hoop edged with iron border

indicators.note: a thing edged with something has it on both sides, so the iron letters go round the hoop

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A metal hoop has an iron rim fitted round it as a border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoop' and 'iron' read as hardware, but 'edged with' means the iron symbol sits on both sides of the hoop word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is an outer edge or margin, as in the fringe of a town.

clue.text: Cheerful flower, colloquially speaking

definitions.meaning: the gladiolus is informally shortened in Britain

explanation.surface: A bright bloom, chatted about casually, lifts the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy and pleased mean the same; the gladiolus flower has an informal shortened name, and both senses use the same four letters.

clue.text: Vehicle turned up before another at game

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for the vehicle is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
another vehicle, so a car
taken as written

explanation.surface: One car arrives just ahead of another at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses CAB to BAC; 'another' means another vehicle, CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game played for stakes.

clue.text: Precise and meticulous record

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to write down the proceedings of a meeting

explanation.surface: A careful clerk keeps an exact, thorough account.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective (said my-NEWT) means exact or scrupulous; the noun or verb means the written record of a meeting.

clue.text: Nervous mishit giving leg slip a chance

definitions.text: mishit giving leg slip a chance
definitions.meaning: in cricket a batter's mishit off the edge of the bat can fly to a fielder in a slip position

explanation.surface: An anxious cricketer's poor shot offers a catch to a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg slip is a fielding position close behind the batter on the leg side, waiting for a ball that comes off the bat's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and jumpy is an idiom for anxious; an edged shot comes off the side of the bat, making a catchable chance.

clue.text: Shocking way to return to regular beat

definitions.text: Shocking way to return to regular beat

parts.words: Shocking way to return to regular beat
parts.note: reads like a scandalous route back to a police patrol, but describes an electric shock that restores a normal heartbeat

explanation.surface: A police officer gets back to the usual patrol route by outrageous means.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors use an electric pulse to stop a fibrillating heart so its normal rhythm can restart.

clue.text: Did some artwork that could transform any decor

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be transformed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone did a little painting that might change the look of any room's decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could transform' rearranges the eight letters of ANY DECOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured with wax drawing sticks is one kind of artwork, like a child drawing.

definitions.meaning: Cowes Week is a sailing regatta held on the Solent, the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland, so the yachts are in that water

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN SOLENT: the Solent is the stretch of sea off the Isle of Wight where the Cowes Week regatta is sailed.

clue.text: Courses making heavy demand, from what we hear

indicators.note: this phrase signals that the word for a heavy demand is sounded out, not spelt

parts.note: to tax is to make a heavy demand on, as in taxing one's patience

explanation.surface: Some courses ask a great deal of students, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests lessons, but the definition is the sailing sense: the zigzag legs a boat takes into the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat changes direction in a series of legs, so these are lines of travel or directions taken.

clue.text: Part of film, limited edition, was staggering

parts.note: a reel is one spool of a film
edition cut short gives its abbreviation ED

explanation.surface: A short film released in a limited edition was astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited edition' sounds like a collector's term, but 'limited' just trims edition to ED. 'Staggering' reads as amazing, but means lurching about.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurch or sway unsteadily on one's feet is to reel.

clue.text: Concealed difficulties found in other across answers

definitions.meaning: hidden snags, traps not seen at first
each other across answer conceals a kind of fish, a fisherman's catch: BRILL, RAY, RUDD, SOLE, EEL, GAR, PIKE, LING, DAB and HAKE

explanation.surface: Secret snags lurk inside the rest of the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theme clue: every other across answer holds a fish's name in its letters, such as the sole inside INSOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a snag or drawback, so unseen snags are concealed problems; the second reading is literal fish netted out of sight.

clue.text: Getting in charge

parts.note: entry is the act of getting in
a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Someone is taking control of a situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting in charge' reads as taking command, but split it: the charge for getting in.
explanation.definitionFit: The price paid for admission to a venue or event is a charge for getting in.

clue.text: Notice about horse and cow sounded asinine

indicators.note: the word for notice goes about, so around, the other pieces

parts.note: to heed is to notice
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse
to cow is to intimidate, to awe

explanation.surface: A notice about a horse and a cow made a farmer sound foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the notice word round the horse and cow pieces. Horse is slang for heroin. 'Asinine' looks like 'stupid' but literally means donkey-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine literally means like an ass, and a donkey's bray is its call.

clue.text: Aspect of literacy centrally flawed in three Rs

definitions.meaning: a skill in reading and writing
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; only the first truly starts with R, so the middle one, writing, is misspelt

explanation.surface: One part of being able to read and write is weak at the heart of basic schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' (reading, writing, arithmetic) is a phrase for basic schooling; the joke is that 'writing' has its letters wrong in the slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting words' letters right is part of being literate; the slogan's middle R gets that wrong.

clue.text: Indians bound to cover India on radio

India is the radio alphabet word for I

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as obliged, but it is a leap, HOP. The Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of north-eastern Arizona, once called Indians.

clue.text: Lambs, for example, in Kansas are mixed with sheep

indicators.note: the letters of the words are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: In Kansas, lambs are kept together with the rest of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' shuffles KANSAS ARE with SHEEP. 'Lambs' looks ovine, but means Charles and Mary Lamb, who wrote Tales from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles and Mary Lamb retold the Bard's plays for children, so they are scholars and devotees of his work.
